outcomes.name: The impact of the change has been identified and understood
outcomes.description: There is a clear understanding of who and what will be affected by the change, including impacts on people, processes, roles, responsibilities, services, customers, stakeholders and business-as-usual operations.

outcomes.name: Impacts have been assessed, validated and prioritised
outcomes.description: The scale, complexity, significance and variability of change impacts have been assessed and validated with affected stakeholders, enabling prioritisation of support and planning activity.

outcomes.name: Change impacts are actively managed through plans, governance and support
outcomes.description: Impact insight is used to shape change plans, communications, engagement, learning, risk management, governance decisions and sustainment activity throughout the change lifecycle.

actions.action: Recognise that the change is likely to affect people, processes, services, roles and ways of working.
Begin discussions with leaders and stakeholders regarding who or what may be affected by the change.
Identify high-level business areas, services, teams and stakeholder groups likely to experience change impacts.
Explore stakeholder perceptions of where change may affect their roles, activities or responsibilities.
Identify potential areas of disruption, opportunity or uncertainty associated with the change.
Gain initial agreement that change impact assessment activities will be required.
Begin raising awareness that different stakeholder groups may be affected in different ways.
Review previous change initiatives to identify common impact themes, challenges and lessons learned.
Identify and document the areas, services, teams, roles, processes and stakeholder groups affected by the change.
Develop an initial structured change impact assessment covering people, process, technology, information, governance and ways of working.
Identify and document intended and unintended impacts that could affect performance, service continuity or stakeholder experience.
Assess initial risks arising from identified change impacts.
Define the impact assessment methodology, criteria, measures and evidence sources to be used.
Engage affected stakeholder groups to understand current ways of working and expected impacts.
Assess stakeholder concerns, support requirements, perceived disruption and areas of uncertainty.
Map affected processes, services and ways of working at a level sufficient to assess change impact.
Assess existing pain points, bottlenecks, duplication, workarounds and service pressures that may influence the scale of impact.
Define and establish baseline measures that will enable comparison between current and future states.
Complete a detailed change impact assessment across affected business areas, services, teams and roles.
Assess the scale of impact using agreed criteria such as complexity, frequency, number of people affected and degree of difference from current ways of working.
Translate significant change impacts into change risks, issues or mitigations where appropriate.
Review assessed impacts through appropriate governance routes so that decisions are informed by change impact evidence.
Identify dependencies that could affect impact management, including process, workforce, system, policy, operational or external dependencies.
Validate identified impacts with affected stakeholders and subject matter experts.
